review_rounds.summary: B1 (BLOCKING): every audit event the S4 code tries to write (declaration_context.upserted, precursor.added, precursor.removed) was silently refused by audit_events_insert_own_org_as_self's own event_type allowlist -- a catalog entirely separate from, and never widened alongside, the aggregate_type CHECK constraint the schema migration DID widen. The dossier had no audit trail at all. B2 (BLOCKING): an ordinary MEMBER of the owning org -- not a stranger -- could UPDATE a declared verifier-report claim or DELETE a declared precursor outright on a record whose parent emission_data row had already gone ACTIVE+VERIFIED; only the application layer (verifyEmissionDataEditable) enforced the post-verification lock, with no database-layer backstop, unlike the established two-wall pattern the parent table's own lock (app.enforce_emission_data_lineage_lock) already uses. Both live-reproduced against real Postgres inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK transactions. Seven non-blocking findings also reported: N1 (getDeclarationContextById/listPrecursorsById intentionally non-throwing on error, an asymmetry with their throwing siblings the review judged not fully justified), N2 (Buyer view's ReadinessCard hardcodes a 'reviewed internally' claim instead of calling the shared reviewBadgeFor helper ProvenanceCard uses two cards above), N3 (ReadOnlyContext ignores the verifierReportDeclared/usesPurchasedPrecursors booleans when deciding whether to show 'no context captured'), N4 (the verification-prose-scan allowlist's own order-dependent substring-stripping bug, independently confirmed by this review -- already being remediated in a separate, independent session per explicit standing instruction not to duplicate that work here), N5/N6/N7 (lower-priority polish items).

review_rounds.b1_resolved: CONFIRMED_FIXED -- independently reproduced as a genuine ordinary MEMBER (real JWT claims, not a service-role shortcut): all three event types now ADMITTED where previously refused; a made-up fourth event type outside the catalog remains correctly REFUSED, confirming the catalog is still a real allowlist, not disabled. Set-diffed the live policy against its pre-widening definition: 39 original values carried forward verbatim, exactly 3 added, 0 dropped.
review_rounds.b2_resolved: CONFIRMED_FIXED -- on a fresh ACTIVE+VERIFIED record, the same ordinary MEMBER was refused on: UPDATE of the verifier-report claim, UPDATE of the process-description text, DELETE of the context row, DELETE of the precursor row, UPDATE of a precursor figure, a same-value no-op UPDATE (proving the lock isn't merely a diff-check), and repointing emission_data_id at a different row (both a DRAFT->DRAFT repoint and a locked->unlocked repoint, proving immutability is independent of lock state). DRAFT-record editing was confirmed unaffected (UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT on an unlocked record all still admitted). A decisive on/off control -- disabling only the new trigger, confirming the same UPDATE that had just been refused was now admitted, then re-enabling it and confirming refusal returned -- proves this specific mechanism, not some other factor, is what closes B2.
review_rounds.bypass_hunt: Adversarially tried and found refused: data-modifying CTEs (UPDATE and DELETE), UPDATE...FROM, MERGE (both update and delete forms), session_replication_role=replica, DISABLE TRIGGER, DROP TRIGGER, replacing the trigger function, TRUNCATE. The migration's own claimed exemption for a cascade-delete-of-the-parent path was verified sound by checking the actual RLS surface: emission_data and organizations have no DELETE policy at all for any authenticated role (not even OWNER/ADMIN), so that path is not reachable by a real caller today. Confirmed the lock also binds service_role (not just ordinary members), matching the parent table's own all-roles posture -- which is exactly why the test cleanup order had to change in this same commit.
review_rounds.b1_new_capability_check: No new forgery capability introduced by the catalog widening -- org_id/actor_user_id remain pinned by the same WITH CHECK regardless of event_type; actor-spoofing, cross-org writes, SYSTEM-attributed events, and UPDATE/DELETE on an existing event were all still refused (audit_events remains append-only).

post_review_remediation.rationale: 5fa5ddf changes exactly one file: a test-only afterAll cleanup-ordering fix (delete the FK-blocking audit_events rows before the organizations delete, and surface that delete's own error instead of swallowing it). No production code, migration, RLS policy, or trigger is touched. This is not the kind of change the standing 'invoke a fresh Opus review' gate (S4 spec section 29) targets -- that gate exists to prevent self-certifying a remediation to a BLOCKING finding against application/security-relevant code, which round 2 already did, independently, against cb5fe2a. Verified directly instead: typecheck clean; the affected test file plus its sibling run clean with zero leaked fixtures across two consecutive runs (confirmed by direct SQL query against the local database, both before and after); the full regression suite (2037 passed / 2 pre-existing failures / 14 skipped) re-run clean afterward. The already-leaked rows from prior runs (10 orgs, 15 audit_events rows, 5 auth users, accumulated before this fix existed) were manually purged from the local database as part of this remediation. N2-N4 are genuine but non-blocking, none crosses a tenant boundary or shows a wrong regulatory figure -- the two classes of finding this codebase treats as blocking -- and are recorded below as known, disclosed, deferred gaps rather than fixed silently or left implicit.

known_open_gaps: N2 -- app.enforce_dossier_lock is SECURITY INVOKER and reads the parent emission_data row through the caller's own RLS visibility; if that lookup ever finds no row for a reason OTHER than a legitimate same-transaction cascade delete of the parent, the lock fails open rather than closed. Not reachable today (child.org_id is pinned to the parent's own immutable entered_by_org_id, and emission_data_id is now immutable on both dossier tables), but a SECURITY DEFINER lookup or an explicit fail-closed branch would remove the assumption entirely rather than rely on it staying true.

N3 -- docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md's audit-event catalog table does not list the three new S4 event types (declaration_context.upserted, precursor.added, precursor.removed), now that they are actually writable. A documentation gap, not a behavioral one.

N4 -- a new precursor can still be INSERTed against an already ACTIVE+VERIFIED record at the database layer (app.enforce_dossier_lock only fires on UPDATE/DELETE), matching the parent table's own 'evidence may only grow' posture. The application layer's own DRAFT-only gate (verifyEmissionDataEditable) is the only wall preventing this via the UI/Server Actions today. Since Buyer view (get-buyer-view.ts) reads live, unfrozen data, a direct-API caller could append free-text precursor content to a record a buyer may already be viewing. Worth an explicit decision (accept as consistent with the existing evidence-growth model, or add a second wall) rather than leaving it as an unstated assumption.

N1 (round 1, deferred) -- getDeclarationContextById/listPrecursorsById remain intentionally non-throwing on a genuine fetch error, an asymmetry with their org-scoped throwing siblings (getDeclarationContext/listPrecursors, fixed in 662d843). summary: PASS_WITH_NOTES. Two independent, fresh Opus reviews were run against this phase, in isolated worktrees with no shared context between them, with each other, or with the implementing session. The first (round 1, against 949afcf) found the phase's tenant-isolation and sharing-RLS work sound but returned FAIL on two BLOCKING findings, both live-reproduced against real Postgres: B1, a complete absence of an audit trail for the entire dossier feature, because the audit event catalog allowlist was never widened to admit the three new event types (a different, separate gate from the aggregate-type CHECK that WAS widened); and B2, no database-layer lock on a published dossier claim once its parent record reached ACTIVE+VERIFIED -- only an application-layer check stood in the way, unlike the established two-wall pattern the parent table's own lock already uses. Both were remediated in cb5fe2a via a new migration (20260906200000) that widens the audit catalog and adds app.enforce_dossier_lock, mirroring the parent table's own durable-marker design one level down, plus emission_data_id immutability on both dossier tables. Before committing, this session independently live-reproduced both fixes itself, via real BEGIN...ROLLBACK transactions, matching the review's own methodology, and confirmed both closed. The second review (round 2, against cb5fe2a, a different agent instance with no knowledge of round 1's own agent) independently reproduced the same two closures itself, ran a dedicated adversarial bypass hunt against the new lock's own stated design assumptions (cascading deletes, CTEs, MERGE, trigger-disabling, replication-role tricks) and found none succeeded, confirmed the audit-catalog widening introduced no new forgery capability, and returned PASS / CERTIFIABLE: YES with zero new blocking findings and four new non-blocking ones (N1-N4). N1 -- that the new B1 regression tests themselves leaked test fixtures into the shared local database on every run, due to an FK-constraint interaction the test's own cleanup didn't anticipate -- was fixed immediately in the very next commit (5fa5ddf), verified clean across two consecutive runs, and did not warrant a third full review round on its own merits: it changes exactly one test file's cleanup ordering, touches no production code, security boundary, or database policy, and was verified directly via typecheck and the full regression suite rather than by re-invoking the adversarial-review gate that exists specifically to guard against self-certifying fixes to blocking, security-relevant findings. N2-N4 remain open, disclosed, non-blocking gaps, none of which shows a wrong regulatory figure or crosses a tenant boundary -- the two classes of finding this codebase treats as blocking. P14's protected regulatory zone and protected P14 product behavior were both confirmed untouched across the entire phase. The D2 authorization gate was respected throughout: never inferred, never built. No S5 work was started. This certification authorizes nothing beyond the review itself: no merge, no deploy. Push of this certified state to origin/feature/sme-experience is authorized per the governing spec's own standing instruction (push only, after S4 PASS).
